\section*{Nurture SRG papers}
\begin{bankq}[id=NSRG03-P1-PHY-S1-Q02, source={Nurture SRG - Test 03 (04 Feb 2024)}, paper=1, qno=2, type=single, subtopic={Kinetic theory}, answer={A}, answer_src=key, difficulty=4, diff_parts={K1 S2 I1 C1 F0}, diff_note={concepts: pressure from the speeds of particles in a container | steps: pressure formula in terms of mean square speed; sum of squares weighted by number; value of PV}]
A sealed cubical container with volume $V$ contains 20 particles each of mass $m$ but having various speeds. Two particles have speed $V$, three particles have speed $2V$, five particles have speed $3V$, four particles have speed $4V$, three particles have speed $5V$, two particles have speed $6V$ and one has speed $7V$. If the pressure exerted by these particles on the walls of container is $P$, then $PV$ is equal to
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{$\dfrac{319}3mv^2$}
\opt{B}{$\dfrac83mv^2$}
\opt{C}{$\dfrac{51}3mv^2$}
\opt{D}{$\dfrac{20}3mv^2$}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=NSRG03-P2-PHY-S1-Q02, source={Nurture SRG - Test 03 (04 Feb 2024)}, paper=2, qno=2, type=single, subtopic={Gas laws}, answer={C}, answer_src=solved, working={Gas pressure doubles at fixed volume, outside pressure $P_0$: tension $=(2P_0-P_0)A=P_0A$}, difficulty=4, diff_parts={K1 S2 I1 C1 F0}, diff_note={concepts: tension in a wire between two pistons | steps: pressure of the heated gas; force on each piston; tension}]
A cylindrical tube of cross-sectional area $A$ has two air tight frictionless pistons at its two ends. The pistons are tied with a straight piece of metallic wire. The tube contains a gas at atmospheric pressure $P_0$ and temperature $T_0$, If temperature of the gas is doubled then the tension in the wire is\par
\bfig{72.5}{NSRG03_p2_phy_s1_q02_1.png}
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{$4P_0A$}
\opt{B}{$P_0A/2$}
\opt{C}{$P_0A$}
\opt{D}{$2P_0A$}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=NSRG03-P2-PHY-S2-Q06, source={Nurture SRG - Test 03 (04 Feb 2024)}, paper=2, qno=6, type=multi, subtopic={Molecular speeds}, answer={C,D}, answer_src=solved, working={$v_p<v_{av}<v_{rms}$ and $\tfrac32kT=\tfrac34mv_p^2$; the distribution has no upper or lower cutoff}, difficulty=5, diff_parts={K1 S2 I2 C0 F1}, diff_note={concepts: speeds of molecules in a gas | steps: ordering of the characteristic speeds; range of speeds; kinetic energy in terms of the most probable speed}]
Let $v_{av}$, $v_{rms}$ and $v_p$ respectively denote mean speed, root mean square speed and the most probable speed of the molecule in an ideal monoatomic gas at absolute temperature $T$. The mass of a molecule is $m$ then :
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{No molecule can have speed greater than $\sqrt2\,v_{rms}$}
\opt{B}{No molecule can have speed less than $\dfrac{v_p}{\sqrt2}$}
\opt{C}{$v_p<v_{av}<v_{rms}$}
\opt{D}{The average kinetic energy of a molecule is $\dfrac34mv_p^2$}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}

\section*{TOAS papers}
\begin{bankq}[id=TOAS13-P1-PHY-S1-Q04, source={TOAS - Test 13 (24 Jul 2022)}, paper=1, qno=4, type=multi, subtopic={Kinetic theory}, answer={A,B,C,D}, answer_src=key, difficulty=3, diff_parts={K2 S1 I0 C0 F1}, diff_note={concepts: partial pressure and moles, kinetic theory | steps: mole ratio from masses and molar masses; compare pressure, number, KE per molecule and rms speed}]
A closed vessel contains a mixture of two diatomic gases A and B. Molar mass of A is 16 times that of B and mass of gas A, contained in the vessel is 2 times that of B :-
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{Pressure exerted by gas B is eight times that of exerted by gas A.}
\opt{B}{Number of molecules of gas B in the cylinder is eight times that of gas A.}
\opt{C}{Average kinetic energy per molecule of gas A is equal to that of gas B.}
\opt{D}{Root mean square value of translational speed of gas B is four times that of A.}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=TOAS13-P2-PHY-S1-Q10, source={TOAS - Test 13 (24 Jul 2022)}, paper=2, qno=10, type=single, subtopic={Kinetic theory}, answer={B}, answer_src=key, difficulty=1, diff_parts={K1 S1 I0 C0 F0}, diff_note={concepts: energy conservation when mixing ideal gases | steps: T = (N1 T1 + N2 T2)/(N1 + N2) = 240 K}]
Two different perfect monoatomic gases at absolute temperature 300 K and 200 K having number of molecules $2\times10^{18}$ and $3\times10^{18}$ are mixed in a container of negligible heat capacity. Temperature of mixture is :
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{210 K}
\opt{B}{240 K}
\opt{C}{260 K}
\opt{D}{280 K}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=TOAS14-P1-PHY-S3-Q05, source={TOAS - Test 14 (07 Aug 2022)}, paper=1, qno=5, type=numerical, subtopic={Kinetic theory}, answer={2}, answer_src=key, difficulty=7, diff_parts={K2 S2 I2 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: kinetic theory momentum transfer, mean molecular speed | steps: mean speed from RT/M; momentum given to the moving face from the relative velocity; drag force as density times area times v0 times mean speed}]
Consider a rectangular block of wood moving with velocity $v_0=5$m/s in a gas at temperature $27^\circ$C and mass density 2 kg/m$^3$. Velocity of block is perpendicular to it's face having area $A=1$ cm$^2$. Find drag force (in N) on the block of molar mass of gas is 10 g/mol $\left(R=\dfrac{25}{3}\dfrac{\text J}{\text{mol K}}\right)$.
\end{bankq}
